findings.cause: A live HA TTS request contained 980 ms and 920 ms internal quiet intervals. Its longest exact digital-zero runs were 657.7 ms and 681.8 ms. Full decode arrived within 354 ms of first decoded audio; this was provider PCM silence, not a corresponding network gap.
findings.repair: Cap only internal runs of exact-zero PCM at 450 ms. Preserve every nonzero sample, leading and trailing PCM, text and cancellation. No global rate change.

findings.cause: The native adapter ended a wire generation after 300 ms of quiet even inside a known literal answer. The next sentence waited for FINISHED, reprised the 100 ms priming lead and re-entered a bounded leading-audio buffer.
findings.repair: A token binds a literal speech part to one native playback generation. Internal pauses and quiet continuations remain inside it; explicit end flushes, waits for the actual receipt and preserves STOP. A stale token cannot flush a newer part.
findings.reason: No new evidence justifies increasing the existing 550 ms transcript debounce. Prior input fixes and tests remain valid within their original bounds.

findings.cause: The inherited speaker session checked core readiness before local wake, allowing a temporary core outage to eject a passive standby socket.
findings.repair: Keep the same connection-local ICE prewarm while waiting for fresh local wake and checking authority. Only then use the unchanged core admission/capture/lease flow. Failure before handoff also closes the prewarmed media.
findings.limits: Active-disconnect cleanup and fresh admission already passed in the baseline; they are preserved, not claimed as a newly fixed bug.

findings.finding: Pinned XMOS v1.3.1 maps channel 0 to the processed AGC path with AEC and uses I2S as its reference. Native output uses the same mixer/I2S speaker. No wrong-channel or reference bypass was proven.
findings.nextRequiredEvidence: Labelled acoustic capture with actual speaker playback and a person speaking over it. Do not remove the native echo fence based only on firmware defaults or simulated receipts.
